meta.title: React Router
meta.description: Framework mode: the loader holds the items, the route renders them, the URL carries the day.

goal: Render the schedule in a React Router application in framework mode, with the day in the URL and the items in a loader. This documentation site is built that way, so the pattern here is the one it uses.

points: A React Router 7 or 8 project in framework mode, with or without server rendering.
A route to put the schedule on.

install.title: Install the package
install.text: One dependency; the router stays yours.

stylesheet.title: Import the stylesheet in the root route
stylesheet.text: The root route’s module is loaded for every page, which makes it the right place for a global stylesheet. With server rendering on, the import is also what puts the CSS in the document rather than in a later chunk.

route.title: Load the items, render the schedule
route.text: The loader is where the fetching belongs. Returning the date alongside the items keeps the render deterministic: the same URL renders the same schedule on the server and in the browser.

range.title: Follow the rendered range
range.text: onVisibleRangeChange fires on mount and whenever the range moves. Writing that range back into the URL lets the loader refetch, which keeps the back button and a shared link honest.

result.text: A route that renders the day in its URL, refetches when the reader moves to another shift, and survives a reload with the same schedule on screen.

points: A loop of fetches: the range change writes a URL that loads items that change the range. Write only the date, and only when it differs from the one already there.
The scroll position jumps on every navigation: pass preventScrollReset, as the snippet above does.
With ssr: false and prerendering, the schedule is rendered at build time; pass now so the prerendered frame and the browser agree.
